title: Franz Paul von Lisola → Leopold, King of Hungary and Bohemia, Dankow: report with cipher the editor found not deciphered (Pribram no. LX)
correspondents: Franz Paul von Lisola (imperial envoy) → the Emperor / court of Vienna
shelfmark: Vienna, ÖStA HHStA, Staatenabteilungen, Polen I (Polonica), Karton 69 (02.1657-08.1657): Lisola's report of 3 Jun 1657; printed in part by Pribram, Archiv für österreichische Geschichte 70 (1887), no. LX
folio_note: About one and a half pages and two lines of cipher without decipherment, in three places of the report (Pribram p. 284-285). The Karton is assigned from the AIS date ranges; the report is not itemised in the AIS and Pribram gives no folio.
status: Pribram printed the report from the original in the Vienna Staatsarchiv and notes: "Zum Theile nicht dechiffrirt ... Folgt eine halbe Seite nicht dechiffrirt ... Folgt ungefähr eine nicht dechiffrirte Seite ... Folgen zwei Zeilen nicht dechiffrirt". The clear and contemporaneously deciphered parts are printed; the passages he names had no decipherment with them. Not on DECODE (searched 11 Nov 2026).
why: Lisola's assessment of Charles X Gustav's plans after the Danish declaration of war, days after the Austro-Polish alliance: the unread passages follow his forecast of a Swedish strike through Silesia.
score_note: Scored from the printed edition during the 11 Nov 2026 printed-series sweep (research/sweep_2026-11-11_printed_series/); original not viewed
verify: Order the leaf from HHStA (Polen I Karton 69; if not there, Brandenburgica or Suecica of the same months). Lisola's other reports of 1655-60 in the same Kartons carry contemporary decipherments (Pribram prints them between asterisks), so the key can be rebuilt from siblings.
prior_art: open (checked 11 Nov 2026: Pribram's edition opened and says not deciphered; DECODE, cryptiana, web searches)
access_note: Not digitised: HHStA reading room or a scan order; Karton-level record only.

folio_note: Two despatches; 'grösstentheils undechiffrirt' and 'zum grossen Theil nicht dechiffrirt'
status: Editor (Simson, UA II): 27 July 1667 "Grösstentheils undechiffrirt"; 24 Aug 1667 "Zum grossen Theil nicht dechiffrirt. Vgl. Mignet II p. 285". The printed text is the clear part only. Lionne's office normally deciphered incoming despatches, so a decipherment may lie elsewhere in the volume. DECODE has two Millet letters of 1665 from Poland (R2679, R2681, Mélanges de Colbert), a different mission.
why: French soundings of the Great Elector during the War of Devolution (Rhine alliance, the offer of Guelders, the Polish crown).
